chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from them (peace be upon them), who said:

Do not eat from what is found in the camel, the cow, the sheep, and other animals whose meat is permissible — the genitals with what is in them, their exterior and interior, and the penis, and the two testicles, and the placenta (which is the place of the birth), and the spleen because it is blood, and the glands along with the veins, and the brain/marrow, and that which is found in the loins, and the gallbladder, and the eyeballs, and the cord/nodule that is found in the brain, and the blood.

key_terms.الطِّحَالُ: spleen (forbidden specifically because it is considered blood)
key_terms.الْخَرَزَةُ: cord or nodule (spinal cord material in the brain)
key_terms.الْغُدَدُ: glands (lymph nodes and other glandular tissue)
key_terms.الْمَشِيمَةُ: placenta (the organ connecting the fetus to the womb)

ai.seo_question: What parts of a halal animal are forbidden to eat according to the Imams of Ahlulbayt?
ai.summary: This hadith enumerates specific internal organs and body parts of halal animals that are forbidden (haram) to consume. The ruling is transmitted from the Imams of Ahlulbayt and covers a comprehensive list including reproductive organs, the spleen (explicitly noted as blood), glands, veins, brain matter, gallbladder, eyeballs, spinal cord material, and blood itself. This represents Shia fiqh's detailed jurisprudential tradition of specifying exactly which parts of an otherwise-permissible animal are still forbidden, distinguishing Shia jurisprudence's thoroughness in dietary law.
